answer: Timed distance attestation. Each identity must periodically prove physical presence at a real location by sampling a signed challenge from a quartz clock beacon, then reporting a value derived from that beacon and its own clock within a narrow horizon. Beacons sit at fixed points, each with a distinct coded pulse rate, spread across a meadow and other terrain. A single operator cannot be in two places within the window, so each identity consumes real travel time. Cost: one distinct beacon visit per identity per epoch, plus spoofed-location failure risk.
